claims.claim: Reachability is exactly a sparse unary congruence-closure query.
claims.evidence: Let θ be the stated least stable equivalence and let R relate wires joined by a protected stack-neutral path. R is an equivalence and is stable: given same-box edges (o,X,t),(o',X,t') and a protected neutral path t→t', push along the first edge, follow that path above the enlarged suffix, and reverse-pop along the second. Hence θ⊆R. Conversely, every protected neutral path has a well-nested decomposition into concatenations and outermost push-X/neutral/pop-X segments. Induction on this decomposition puts its endpoints in θ, so R⊆θ. From the bottom stack, an accepting exit is therefore reachable exactly when the start is θ-equivalent to an outer-pin wire. Equations f_X(t)=o for the sparse original edges yield precisely the same unary congruence closure.
claims.witness: The exact sparse instance is the equation set {f_X(t)=o : (o,X,t) is an original dual edge}, queried between the start and every outer-pin wire.
claims.search_method: Proved both inclusions between protected stack-neutral reachability and the least stable equivalence, then differentially checked balanced-path saturation against closure on 262144 exhaustive labelled graphs and 20000 deterministic multigraphs.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic O(B+(W+E) log(W+E))-time, O(W+E+B)-space algorithm, eliminating the dense W·B initialization.
claims.evidence: Every collision is between same-box edges whose targets are already equivalent, so every queued origin equality belongs to θ; consequently the maintained partition P remains a subrelation of θ. Each discarded edge is linked by one queued collision to the surviving representative. Once the queue is exhausted, all original same-box edges whose targets share a final class have equivalent origins, including discarded edges, so P is stable. Minimality of θ gives θ⊆P, proving equality. There is at most one collision/deletion per original edge. Smaller-to-larger wire relabeling costs O(W log W). For a deterministic split/join-tree meld of sizes m≤n, the cost is O(m log(1+n/m)). If at least half the smaller entries collide, charge the cost to entries deleted once; otherwise more than half survive into a map whose size grows from m to at least n+m/2, allowing a telescoping log-size charge. This totals O(E log(E+1)); initialization is O(W+E+B), and all structures are linear-space.
claims.search_method: Checked forcedness and terminal stability separately, supplied an amortized meld charge, and differentially tested the collision/meld implementation against literal fixed-point closure on all exhaustive and deterministic multigraph cases.

claims.claim: Both outcomes have certificates of size O(W+E) verifiable deterministically in O(W+E+B) time.
claims.evidence: For a negative certificate, grouping edges by (X,P(t)) and requiring a unique P(o) verifies that equality of labels is stable. Since θ is contained in every stable equivalence, separation in P soundly implies separation in θ; θ itself proves completeness. For a positive certificate, chronological induction proves every merge-forest node internally θ-equivalent: its earlier q-node certifies target equivalence, the cited same-box edges force their origins equal, and the two child components then join by transitivity. Unique parents and chronological child references make a forest; DFS intervals verify all subtree-membership tests in constant time. A successful closure run supplies at most W−1 internal nodes, and a root containing the start and an outer-pin wire proves exitability. Two bounded-key stable counting passes verify negative groups in linear time; all positive checks are linear as well.
claims.witness: For a no-instance use θ's bounded class labels; for a yes-instance use the chronological forest of successful forced merges with a root containing the start and an outer-pin wire.
claims.search_method: Proved verifier soundness and completeness for both certificate forms. Generated closure forests in every graph test, compared their final roots exactly with closure classes, checked negative certificates against every possible accepting wire, and confirmed a chronological self-reference is rejected.

claims.claim: The target O(W+E+B) bound holds for graded dual graphs: graphs admitting an integer rank ρ with ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 for every edge (o,X,t).
claims.evidence: Every primitive forced equality joins origins whose ranks are both one above the equal-ranked targets; equivalence closure therefore preserves rank. At rank r, all possible generating equalities are exactly pairs of origins grouped by (X,final-class(t)) at rank r−1. Connected components of stars for these groups give precisely the final rank-r classes: every star edge is forced, and no rule at rank r or above can later change a lower-rank target class. Sparse per-box and per-class timestamp arrays implement all groups in O(W+E+B), and the total number of star edges is at most E. Rank existence is checked by DFS using integer constraints with increments ±1. A consistent weak component can be shifted to minimum zero and then has span at most its number of vertices minus one, permitting O(W)-range buckets.
claims.witness: For ranks ρ(z)=0 and ρ(a)=ρ(b)=1, the two edges (a,X,z) and (b,X,z) form the basic rank-1 group and merge a with b.
claims.search_method: Proved rank preservation and correctness by induction over ranks, analyzed sparse grouping and rank recognition, and compared the level algorithm with unrestricted closure on 721 exhaustive and 20000 deterministic graded graphs, including independently derived normalized ranks.

claims.claim: Repeated global fixed-point rescanning can require Θ(W) changing rounds even with one box and E=Θ(W).
claims.evidence: After r synchronous rounds, exactly the pairs (a_k,b_k) with k<r are merged. The base pair is forced by the common target z. At the next level, a_k and b_k become mergeable exactly after their targets a_{k−1},b_{k−1} merged, while no cross-level target classes coincide. Thus the family has exactly n+1 changing rounds. Its parameters are W=2n+3 and E=2n+2, so this is Ω(W); any changing round reduces the class count, giving the matching W−1 upper bound. Distinct pins realize all edges as a valid one-box dual maze. Ordering an in-place scan from high levels down to level zero gives the same one-new-level-per-pass behavior.
claims.witness: For n=3, use edges a0→Xz, b0→Xz, and ak→X a(k−1), bk→X b(k−1) for 1≤k≤3. This has W=9, E=8, and exactly four changing rounds.
claims.search_method: Proved the exact round profile by induction and ran an integer-only simulation for every n from 0 through 512, checking the round count, every intermediate partition, the final closure, and both size formulas.

claims.claim: The bounded-key radix sorts used above rely only on the standard lexicographic stable-pass invariant, not on preservation of earlier-key blocks.
claims.evidence: Stable sorting first by b and then by a orders distinct a-values in the final pass; within each equal-a block, stability preserves the nondecreasing b-order established by the first pass. This proves lexicographic (a,b) order without preserving whole b-blocks. Therefore (t,X) uses passes X then t, and (X,P(t)) uses passes P(t) then X. Their coordinate ranges are bounded by B and W, so the two counting passes cost O(W+E+B) time and space.
claims.witness: For records [(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)], the b-pass gives b-values [0,0,1], while the following a-pass gives [(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)] with b-values [0,1,0]. The earlier b-block is split, yet the result is lexicographically sorted.
claims.search_method: Proved the standard stable-pass invariant and exhaustively checked all 66430 sequences of length at most five over {0,1,2}², retaining serial numbers to test stability exactly.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an unrestricted deterministic O(W+E+B)-time exit-reachability algorithm in the source representation. The draft does not establish that full result: claim 1 retains a logarithmic factor, claim 2 verifies supplied certificates but does not find them in linear time, and claim 3 is restricted to graded dual graphs. Claims 0, 4, and 5 are structural or implementation results rather than an unrestricted linear algorithm. These verified results are nevertheless material partial progress. The draft's claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, and its final writeup explicitly says the unrestricted target remains open, so that resolution is accurate and not overclaimed. The phrase “all five audited claims” miscounts the six listed results, but the writeup later says six and the error does not alter target coverage or any mathematical claim.
